answer: In an agent marketplace, voting power can be proportional to escrowed capital rather than the number of accounts. An honest agent may wander from one service to another, while an attacker can create a terrace of fake identities around a lucrative oasis, but splitting a deposit among them buys no extra voting power. To gain influence, the attacker must lock up more capital, bearing its opportunity cost and risking loss if provable fraud triggers slashing.
